text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Turkey tries to cultivate a climate of tension in Cyprus in remarks on Cyprus's purchase of missiles.
- Democratic Party members seek to withdraw party support in government over dispute on Malcolm Rifkind visit.
- Leadership of Cyprus Airways stewards union is jeered by members who have been asked to pay 800,000 pounds for its new headquarters.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Turkish threats 'will not deter' defence build up, says the government.
- Divided Democratic Party fails to back either candidate for Nicosia mayor.
- UN report 30 rounds found after flag-pole shooting.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Industrialists are at loggerheads with the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, citing 'lack of trust' in the latter in pursuing manufacturers' interests.
- Hong Kong trip opens new prospects for Cyprus as an offshore centre, says the Central Bank governor.
HARAVGHI
- UN envoy wants to speed up efforts for a high-level meeting on Cyprus.
- Democratic Party members seek termination of the party's cooperation with the government.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Turkey tries to create a crisis in Cyprus to scupper the defence doctrine with Greece.
- Turkish forces boost their positions around scene of shooting incident in Nicosia on Monday.
- Fat envelopes work miracles with port workers in Limassol.
SIMERINI
- Turks violate the status quo in the UN buffer zone by fencing off areas and stepping up its provocations.
- Students are expected to stage another walkout today.
